facts.raw_span: A 65-year-old woman presented with blurry vision in her right eye for several months
3 recurrent episodes of bilateral iritis occurring during 5 months
amblyopia in the left eye
bilateral posterior chamber intraocular lens
left-sided mastectomy 2.5 years prior
on anastrozole therapy for more than 2 years
Visual acuity: 20/25 OD and 20/150 OS without improvement on pinhole testing
Intraocular pressures were normal
Right eye showed trace conjunctival injection without definite ciliary flush, 2+ fine keratic precipitates, and 1+ cells in the anterior chamber
cystoid macular edema with a yellow spot in the fovea in the right eye
Optical Coherence Tomography (OCT): Right eye showed significant cystoid macular edema and subfoveal fluid
Tests for vasculitis and rheumatologic disorders were within reference limits

concepts.why: Patient presented with recurrent episodes of bilateral iritis and fine keratic precipitates in the right eye
Patient showed significant cystoid macular edema with subfoveal fluid in the right eye on OCT
Patient had an epiretinal membrane in the left eye on dilated fundus examination
Patient had amblyopia in the left eye
Patient was on anastrozole therapy for more than 2 years and presented with cystoid macular edema
Patient had bilateral posterior chamber intraocular lens and presented with recurrent episodes of bilateral iritis
It explains the finding of decreased visual acuity without improvement on pinhole testing, which is consistent with macular edema.

rationales.F02: Bilateral iritis is a strong indicator of uveitis.
rationales.F06: Anastrozole therapy is associated with maculopathy.
rationales.F09: Conjunctival injection and keratic precipitates are indicative of uveitis.
rationales.F10: Cystoid macular edema is a key feature of macular edema.
rationales.F11: OCT scans showing cystoid macular edema support the diagnosis of macular edema.
rationales.F12: Normal tests for vasculitis and rheumatologic disorders reduce the likelihood of uveitis.

frontier_selector.rationale: The patient's history of anastrozole therapy for more than 2 years and the presence of cystoid macular edema with a yellow spot in the fovea in the right eye support Anastrozole-Associated Maculopathy as the most likely diagnosis.
